_source.doctrine: drinking/provenance.py, pinned by tests/test_drinking_provenance.py, and stated on /about/demonstration-data/: real published records are carried as published, named with their publisher, and labelled on screen. Invented data may never carry a real agency, district, farm or owner name. The two halves of this file are the two halves of that sentence.

notes: DELIBERATE EXCLUSION 1 — 'Diversion Canal Growers' is NOT banned. 97-01-NAMES.md records it as not a real-place exposure: it is a generic invented name that was merely aligned to the seed's naming so one demo carries one set of names. Banning it would also collide with 'Diversion Canal', which is protected real geography in the list below.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSION 2 — 'Bottomlands Cattle Co.' is NOT banned. 97-01-NAMES.md records it as not a real-place exposure either: it was simply stale, no longer matching its right's holder after 97-01 renamed San Joaquin Bottomlands Ranch.

SCOPE IS METADATA, NOT A FILTER, for entries with the default match mode 'global'. The scope records where propagation-analysis §0.2 measured the value. A real district name is wrong in ANY column, so the scan matches global entries everywhere and reports an out-of-scope hit louder, not quieter.

A '*' value means the whole scoped column is real published content and is protected wholesale. This is how §0.2's whole-column protections are expressed, because enumerating values nobody measured would be a list that lies.

KNOWN BLIND SPOT, measured 2026-07-31 and currently empty. core/management/commands/seed_merced_details.py::_fill_account_contacts composes accounting_wateraccount.contact_email by slugifying contact_name (lowercase, non-alphanumerics collapsed to '.'), so a real contact string would survive there as 'merced.water.manager@example.com' — a form no case-insensitive substring of 'Merced Water Manager' matches. Checked on both deployments on 2026-07-31: 0 of 11 accounts carry a contact_email on production and 0 of 11 on staging, so no slug form exists to ban. Deliberately NOT listed as banned values, because they are unmeasured strings. Filed as an issue instead.

THE WELL LABELS ARE NOT IN THE SEEDED DEMO, and --explain says so rather than hiding it. The eight '... Ag Well' entries below are ruled protected by 97-01-NAMES.md and live in core/management/commands/seed_merced_operations.py, but seed_merced_parcels_from_selection REPLACES that command's guessed wells — so the 24 wells on staging are named 'Ag well on MER-APN-NNN' and 'Shared ag well (TI-W-n)' (measured 2026-07-31). Their appearance in --explain's 'matching NOTHING' list is correct output, not a broken protection. Do not delete them: they are the standing record of the ruling if that seed path is ever run again.

On the demo as it stands (2026-07-31) no banned span is suppressed by a protected entry — the two halves do not currently overlap on live data. That is the healthy state, not evidence the protected half is inert: run the scan with --explain to see the protected values it matched in live rows, and see tests/test_identity_policy.py for the widened-policy case that proves suppression works.

Merced Irrigation District's abbreviation, with the trailing space that makes it a name prefix rather than a word. Measured in propagation-analysis §0.2: it produced 'MID Atwater Canal Headgate' in surface_pointofdiversion.name, and 55 rows of parcels_parcelledger.description are COMPOSED from that string — so dropping this one prefix is what cleared all 55. Matched SCOPED rather than globally on purpose: a bare three-letter token matched against every text column in the database would fire on ordinary prose (the middle of a word, an abbreviation in a note) and a tripwire that cries wolf is one people learn to ignore.

Expressed as a wildcard rather than 61 enumerated values, because a list of values nobody measured is a list that lies.

WHOLE COLUMN. parcels_parcel.notes — 76 rows of real DWR land-use provenance ('DWR field 2414906 | Pasture (P1) | Merced | source=surface'), verified identical on both sides in §0.2. The word Merced here is the real county, carried as published.

WHOLE COLUMNS. recharge_rechargesite.name and .notes — basin labels and siting notes built from real canal and river geography ('beside the El Nido Canal', 'served by the Merced River diversion'), verified identical on both sides in §0.2. The recharge OPERATOR column is deliberately NOT protected: that is where the real district name was, and it is a banned scope above.

WHOLE COLUMN. geography_boundary.description — the DWR Bulletin 118 basin description, carried as published: 'Valley floor south of the Merced River to the Chowchilla, San Joaquin River on the west, Sierra foothills on the east... served by Merced Irrigation District's canal network'. That last clause is REAL public infrastructure, and 97-02-SUMMARY.md rules it explicitly as one of the eight justified survivors of the Phase 97 sweep (seed_merced_base.py:55): true public geography, not an attribution of invented data. §0.2 protects geography_boundary as a table. Scoped to the description column only, deliberately — the boundary NAME column stays live, so a real district name landing THERE is still caught.

WHOLE COLUMN. datasync_monitoredstation.station_name — real CDEC and DWR station identifiers and state well numbers, carried unaltered as published record. §0.2 verified the monitoring stations identical on both sides.

WHOLE TABLE GROUP. Every drinking_* table — watersystem, systemfacility, samplingpoint, analyte, regulatorylimit, sampleevent, sampleresult, and envirofactscache. This is real published record end to end: the City of Merced's 61 facilities from EPA Envirofacts, 27 sampling points and all 2023-2026 laboratory results from State Water Board DDW and GAMA. The honesty page states the exception in its own words — 'the drinking-water side is deliberately the opposite: genuine published laboratory results under the City of Merced's real name'. §0.2 verified all of it identical on both sides. Phase 97 changed zero files under drinking/.
